Definition: frankincense (from its whiteness or perhaps that of its smoke)
BiblicalUsage: Frankincense is the spice the Bible calls lebownah — white and costly, burned for God alone, and not to be confused with Lebonah the place, which shares its name. In Exodus 30:34, "[these] sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like [weight]:"; and in Leviticus 2:1, "and put frankincense thereon:". In Isaiah 60:6, "The multitude of camels shall cover thee"; and in Jeremiah 6:20, "To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe frankincense is the smell of prayer that God accepts — white, costly, and burned for Him alone. I hold that when the smoke rises without a heart behind it, God says the offerings are not acceptable. My position is that my worship must be pure frankincense, not a show.
